evidence: Cic. Att. 12.19.1: trāns Tiberim hortōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of getting what one sets out to have: friends, a garden, provisions; with money, “buy” (Lewis & Short). Its first sense is “prepare”.

terms.gloss: get, come by (by luck or opportunity)
evidence: Cic. Fam. 3.7.1: cum plūs ōtī nactus erō
terms.comment: Of what comes one’s way rather than what one works for (Lewis & Short): time, a chance, someone to carry a letter.

evidence: Cic. Sen. 4: quam ut adipīscantur omnēs optant
terms.comment: Of what is reached with effort: old age, honours, wisdom.

terms.gloss: get (by asking), have a request granted
terms.comment: What one gets by asking: impetrāvī, “I got what I asked for”.

phrases.latin: plūribus verbīs ad tē scrībam, cum plūs ōtī nactus erō
phrases.english: I’ll write to you at more length when I get more free time

phrases.latin: canis parturiēns cum rogāsset alteram ut fētum in ejus tuguriō dēpōneret, facile impetrāvit
phrases.english: a dog about to have puppies asked another to let her lay her litter in her kennel, and easily got her way

phrases.latin: amīcōs nōn parāre, optimam et pulcherrimam vītae, ut ita dīcam, supellectilem
phrases.english: … and not to get friends, the best and finest furniture of life, so to speak
